key_insight: Combining UMAP with DBSCAN improved unsupervised clustering of breast cancer electronic health record data, making patient-group patterns easier to detect.
clinical_relevance: This approach may help researchers uncover clinically meaningful subgroups in routine breast cancer records for further medical interpretation.
method: Analyzed three independent breast cancer EHR datasets
Applied DBSCAN clustering, then added UMAP dimensionality reduction before clustering
Evaluated clusters with DBCV, DCSI, and DISCO indices
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved clustering performance when UMAP was combined with DBSCAN, supported by three statistical cluster-validity measures.
watch_item: Findings are exploratory and unsupervised, so cluster utility depends on external validation and careful medical interpretation before any real-world use.
paper_title: An unsupervised clustering analysis of breast cancer data derived from electronic health records enhanced through UMAP dimensionality reduction
